Upon arrival, I was informed that there was only one doctor at the clinic, without an assistant, attending to an emergency. I understand that emergencies happen and take priority, but I consider it unacceptable that a clinic that charges high fees for consultations and hospitalization operates with only one doctor, without a support team, making it impossible for other patients and their owners to receive the necessary care.

Furthermore, once again there was a lack of communication. No one came to explain the situation, give an estimated time, or apologize for the delay. I have been waiting for over an hour for a visit with limited time.

I hope you will reconsider this form of service, as the lack of structure and communication has been recurrent throughout Amarelinho's hospitalization. I am bothered by the lack of more complete updates, with explanations about the evolution of the condition, in addition to the sending of photos and videos, which help me to follow the treatment and make me feel more at ease. This would show respect and care for the patient and their owner, and unfortunately, that is not happening.

But in August 2025, I paid for a castration procedure for R$589 via Pix, but I did not have the procedure done due to personal problems. In April 2026, I asked for information about what could be done, and I was informed that the amount would be refunded. But until now, July 12, 2026, I have not received any further response, nor any information. I have already filed a complaint on Reclame Aqui, but I have not received a response either. I went to the store 4 times during this period, and there were many attempts to communicate via WhatsApp. And when I was attended to once by the manager, the service was very good. But that was in May 2026, and until now I have not received any further information about the progress of the refund.

I do not recommend them, and I issue a warning about advance payments, because if the service is not performed, as in my case, the amount will not be refunded. Not even having information about what was offered by the clinic's own manager, in this case the refund.

Terrible clinic. Absolutely unprepared staff, from the receptionist to the veterinarian. I think they work with quotas because they push unnecessary procedures and hospitalizations, only focusing on the financial aspect. They don't care much about life. A real slaughterhouse. I was lucky to get my dog ​​out of there in time because they were killing him due to lack of medication and minimal care. To summarize, my dog ​​left there without his right eye. And that wasn't even why he was hospitalized. It was just a matter of taking him to another veterinarian for proper medication, and the dog is already a different dog; he walks, eats, relieves himself on his own, and is at home.

I took my cat for hospitalization on September 25th, and I had one of the worst possible experiences. The doctor, Ana Carolina, attended to me without professionalism, seemed unwilling to be there, gave me conflicting information, and said the cat would be discharged on Sunday. Then, on Saturday, the doctor, Ana Beatriz, said the opposite, in addition to being mocking, impatient, and unable to clearly explain the situation. Extremely unprepared.

The clinic's communication is chaotic and a complete mess: vague WhatsApp responses like, "your cat is quiet and lethargic," without details, and contradictory new quotes.

The manager never shows up, hides behind the team, and resolves everything by phone. He didn't even have the courage to speak to me in person to clarify what was happening. This omission reflects the chaos and disorganization, and shows that the clinic's focus is only on finances, not animal welfare.

Remember that their role is to explain everything clearly. In the end, I took my cat back on Saturday because the "manager" said he did a check that only he saw, even though I know very well what I heard. There's no credibility at this clinic, and I'm not surprised by the negative reviews on Google.

The only exception was the doctor, Raphael, who demonstrated preparedness, empathy, and professionalism.

Given this, it's clear that the clinic exists solely for profit and that no one there is prepared to deal with the public.

I took my Yorkshire Terrier for a bath and grooming, and to my surprise, the groomer didn't have clippers. We continued anyway, but after bathing her, they interrupted the process, leaving my dog ​​still damp in the cold weather with the air conditioning on. They handed her over to my wife to attend to another dog. After waiting a little over two hours for them to finish with another animal, I gave up and went to pick her up. This kind of attitude is absurd and unprofessional. I'm totally disappointed with the service, and we even had to pay for their incompetence.

It all started when I took my kitten to the Pechincha unit, where they requested additional tests such as X-rays and ultrasound. We were very well attended to by Dr. Carolina, by the way. Immediately, I took him for the X-ray. My cat had a fever when I left Pechincha and, due to the stress of the blood collection, transport, and X-ray, Dr. Raphael, upon leaving the exam, said that my cat was in a pre-convulsive stage and would have to be hospitalized urgently for at least 48 hours, the time it took for the blood test results to be finalized. One detail: The vet who attended him said that it could take 48 hours, but that blood tests were usually ready sooner. When I refused hospitalization, the veterinarian's approach changed: he said that he could resolve the fever spike with intramuscular dipyrone. We returned the following week for the ultrasound. Dr. Bruna, who performed the ultrasound, calmly commented on some of the imaging findings during the examination, justifying some of them due to the recent vaccination. At the end, we were offered a follow-up appointment with Dr. Raphael. We accepted, as the kitten had been lethargic for a week and the previously prescribed medications had already finished. He spoke with the sonographer and, upon returning, once again stated that hospitalization was now essential, as my cat had feline triaditis. Again, I refused to have him hospitalized. He wrote a kind of referral, stating that some symptoms had supposedly been seen in the imaging exam that were not true (I emphasized several times that the cat was eating, and he wrote in this "document" that the cat was already suffering from starvation). He said that if I didn't hospitalize him, I would lose my pet in a short time. I felt as if there was a great need to sell some procedure or hospitalization for commission. It didn't inspire confidence, especially when my husband inquired about what would be done during the hospitalization and the veterinarian gave vague answers. Finally, the next day, the ultrasound report was issued, containing information that did not accurately correspond to what was reported in the referral. It's sad to know that health, in general, has become a commodity. My kitten is doing great now. He was treated correctly by another professional. He didn't need hospitalization.

Complete disappointment with the Gabinal – Freguesia unit.

When we take a pet to the clinic, we take a piece of our heart with us. We expect care, respect, and at the very least, humane treatment. What I found was exactly the opposite: apathetic, cold professionals with no empathy whatsoever—neither for me nor for my animal.

I was seen by a veterinarian (I believe his name is César) who, instead of guiding me attentively and clearly, tried to push a blood test on me, saying it was necessary for vaccination—and then, when I refused the procedure, he “changed his mind” and said he could administer the vaccine anyway. The clear feeling is that it was a forced sale, not a concern for my pet's health.

Furthermore, when I was informed of the price, I was told it was different if I paid via PIX—which is illegal according to current legislation. PIX is money and should be treated as a cash payment.

I left the clinic frustrated, disappointed, and certain that this is not a company that values ​​animal welfare or transparency with pet owners.

This serves as a warning to other clients: be careful with the practices of this establishment. And to the clinic: urgently review the conduct of your staff. Love for animals requires more than a diploma—it requires empathy and ethics.

The price of a consultation is quite reasonable, but everything else, like exams and specialist appointments, is less so. At the first appointment I took my dog ​​to, I felt Dr. Felipe and Dr. Talita were very capable professionals, but their explanation of my pet's problems and the purpose of the exams they ordered was vague. I asked some questions but received vague answers that didn't clear up my doubts. They barely looked at me and talked more amongst themselves about the procedures that should be done than they explained anything to me. They gave my dog ​​some injections that I still don't understand the purpose of. Besides several exams, I ended up being directed to schedule a dermatology appointment with Dr. Talita, even though it wasn't exactly a skin problem, but rather an ear problem. I got a little more information, but I didn't end up trusting the doctors much. That same day was supposed to be the follow-up appointment with Dr. Felipe, but he didn't even want to look at the dog. I understood that Talita had already examined her and could pass on her condition to him, but I found it strange. Furthermore, I was charged for a follow-up appointment with the dermatologist; I've never seen a place charge for a follow-up appointment, even with human doctors (and the price is more expensive than a consultation with a general practitioner). My dog's case required surgery, and I ended up having the surgery done elsewhere; I didn't feel comfortable with the clinic.
